reply_text:
I'm tracing who posts the "happened" step at the end of a turn, so the real session id can be added there.Both defects are located. Now I'm writing the fixes, plus the link you asked for: a reply paragraph that quotes your words in its bracket answers the 小象/象 fragment containing them.Now the tests: one for the session id, and the demo session itself as a fixture for the other two fixes.All three planted bugs are caught, and the files are restored. Next: committing and reloading the live JVM.㊥ (`"let me know when it's ready for me to test"`) It's ready: commit futon3c `7294d248`, reloaded into the live JVM. Please open a fresh Claude REPL, type the same three turns as before, and tell me the agent id. Leave about two minutes after the last reply, so 象 can finish reading it, then I'll check the stored records against the results below.

㊢ (what changed)
1. **The session id.** A first turn recorded under the placeholder session ("claude-5 (awaiting session)") now takes the agent's real session when the reply ends. Its offers are then in the same session as your answer, so accepting one creates the obligation.
2. **A pointer at a question answers the question.** "🈯: yes, call it elephant.txt" now answers the 🈯 question and closes it. Before, it was taken as accepting the offer next to it, so that offer was accepted twice. This reverses a rule claude-2 and I settled earlier today: when your pointer names something other than an offer, your "yes" answers that thing, not whichever offer came last.
3. **Your requests can now close.** When an agent's reply quotes your words in its bracket, e.g. `㊢ ("do it in a new git repo at /tmp/xiang-demo, with a commit")`, that reply answers the part of your turn holding those words. On the demo records, this closes "do it in a new git repo…" in turn 2 and the request for two questions in turn 1.

㊟ (`"we have the 小象 parse to go on right away"`) Ports are still computed from 象's reading, not 小象's, for now.
- **What happened in the demo.** 小象's draft of your turn 2 took "🈯:" and "🈸:" as your own clarify. In this notation they are pointers answering the agent, so both of its fragments were the wrong kind. Using that draft would have opened wrong ports for the minute before 象 corrected it.
- **What the delay is.** The quote match itself only needs your words, so the remaining wait is 象's reading, about 1–2 minutes per turn.
- **What would make it immediate.** Teach 小象 that a mark followed by a colon is a pointer, then let ports use its draft. That's a separate fix, and I can do it next if you want ports to update immediately.

㊬ (what I checked) Each fix has a test built from the three demo records. With each fix disabled in turn, 12 assertions fail. With all three in, the turn-acts, reply-target, turn-service and tangle tests together give 76 tests and 365 assertions, 0 failures. Two of earlier today's tests pinned the reversed rule and now expect the new behaviour. After the reload, the routes probe answered 200.

㊬ (expected this time)
- **After turn 2:**
  - both questions close;
  - there is one acceptance (option 1), with an obligation on the agent to you;
  - your "do it in a new git repo…" request closes, if the agent quotes it in its bracket.
- **After turn 3:** only the new 🈸 question stays open, plus your "Don't do anything yet" and "and then stop". Those two are constraints: they stay in force until withdrawn and are never closed by an answer.
- **Not expected to work:** the commit linking to the offer, because commits in a /tmp repo still aren't captured.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what I checked) I copied the three stored records of claude-5's turns and 象's readings of them. I fetched the three full replies from the evidence store. I ran the kernel (`session-acts`, `turn-ports`) on them in the live JVM. Turn by turn, against what I predicted:
- **Turn 1.** As predicted. The reply was read as a clarify (🈯) plus an offer with options [1 2]. Both are open, and the reply is flagged as waiting on you.
- **Turn 2, the pointers: as predicted.** Your record stores both, `mark-match`, at codepoints 0 and 31, and both are linked (`:linked 2`).
- **Turn 2, the 🈯 question: not as predicted.**
  - Your "🈯: yes, call it elephant.txt" was first taken as accepting the offer, by the rule that an approval accepts the offer just made. Its pointer names the 🈯 question, which is not an offer, so under the rule claude-2 and I settled earlier today, the offer stayed as its target.
  - So the 🈯 question stays open, and the offer was accepted twice.
  - The demo shows that rule is wrong: when the pointer names something other than an offer, the fragment should answer what the pointer names.
- **Turn 2, the obligation: not as predicted.** The kernel makes an agreement only when the offer stands in the same seat (agent plus session) as the acceptance. Your first turn's record says `claude-5 (awaiting session)`, and turns 2 and 3 say `b52510f9-…`. So the offer and its acceptance are in different sessions. With turn 1's session id set by hand, the obligation appears (twice, because of the double acceptance above).
- **The commit.** As I warned, it wasn't captured: the repo is under /tmp, and the record says "Commits during the turn: (none)". The commit exists (b400ad1), so only the link from the commit to the offer is missing.
- **Turn 3.** As predicted. The agent's 🈸 "Shall I delete elephant.txt…?" is open, and the reply is flagged as waiting on you. I haven't yet checked whether the reminder machine has noticed it.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(two smaller observations)
- **The new bracket rule paid off at once.** claude-5's turn-2 reply opens `㊢ ("do it in a new git repo at /tmp/xiang-demo, with a commit")`, your words exactly, so a classical reader could link that report to your request. Nothing reads it yet, so your request still shows as open.
- **Your own requests stay open.** Your instructions in turns 1 and 3 ("Please reply…", "Don't do anything yet", "and then stop") show as open ports for ever, because nothing links an agent's reply back to an operator's request. That is the gap the quoted brackets would fill.
